 2                ACTING PRESIDENT BENJAMIN:   The 

 3   Senate will come to order.  

 4                I ask everyone present to please 

 5   rise and recite the Pledge of Allegiance.

 6                (Whereupon, the assemblage recited 

 7   the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.)

 8                ACTING PRESIDENT BENJAMIN:   Rabbi 

 9   Brian Leiken, of Temple Beth Shalom in New City, 

10   will deliver today's invocation.

11                RABBI LEIKEN:   Sovereign of the 

12   universe, Who created all in love, teach us to 

13   love all that is good and beautiful in this 

14   world.  Teach us to honor the dignity of 

15   difference, recognizing that one who is not in 

16   our image is nonetheless in Your image; never 

17   forgetting that the people not like us are still 

18   people -- like us.

19                At this fateful moment in the human 

20   story, bless us so that we may be a blessing to 

21   others.  Guide the nations of the world to honor 

22   You by honoring one another, so that by reaching 

23   out in love we may turn enemies into friends and 

24   become Your family on earth as You are our parent 

25   in heaven.


                                                                1166

 1                Beloved God, bless the members of 

 2   this New York State Senate.  Guide their 

 3   deliberations, that they may govern this great 

 4   state with wisdom and justice, grace and 

 5   compassion, bringing honor to Your name and Your 

 6   blessing to all of humankind.

 7                Amen.  

 8                (Response of "Amen.")

21   Senator Martinez for an introduction.

22                SENATOR MARTINEZ:   Good morning, 

23   Mr. President, and thank you.  

24                First of all, I would like to take a 

25   moment to thank Senator Brooks for bringing light 


                                                                1168

 1   to dyslexia through the Awareness Day today here 

 2   in Albany.  This is a disorder that many 

 3   experience and a disorder that many don't realize 

 4   exists -- or maybe they don't want to admit that 

 5   it exists.  

 6                I am proud to have today in our 

 7   chambers a young girl who has dyslexia, and she 

 8   has made it her superpower.  Not only is she a 

 9   constituent of mine, but she has volunteered in 

10   my office, which has made her an honorary member 

11   of my team.  

12                Her name is Olivia.  She is a 

13   firecracker who lights up the room.  She walks 

14   into a room and inspires everyone; she lights up 

15   the room as well.  Every single person she comes 

16   in contact with, she puts a smile on their face.  

17   She is always eager to help the community by 

18   giving back, and she's always helping out those 

19   animals that need some help as well.  

20                Nothing will stop this young little 

21   girl from changing the world, especially the 

22   world with dyslexia.  And I for one cannot wait 

23   to see what the future holds for her.  

24                And if you could all indulge me, but 

25   she has written a little bio about herself that I 


                                                                1169

 1   would like to read to the chamber today.  And it 

 2   is titled "How to be Me."  

 3                "Hi, my name is Olivia Nicole 

 4   Ekizian.  I was born and raised on Long Island.  

 5   I love my mommy, daddy, dog Joey and cats Fiona 

 6   and Chloe.  I am an athlete:  I am a dancer, an 

 7   equestrian, and I am on the swim team.  

 8                "I have dyslexia, which means I 

 9   learn differently, I think differently, and it 

10   makes me special.  It can help me in math.  

11   Instead of using graph paper, I can do it in my 

12   head.  I am very good with my hands and 

13   electronics, like I like LEGOs.  And I like 

14   bracelet-making and doing my hair and others' 

15   hair as well.  

16                "I am in fourth grade at Sycamore 

17   Elementary School.  Spelling and social studies 

18   are what comes hard to me the most.  When I grow 

19   up, I want to be a judge, a horseback riding 

20   trainer, a hair designer, or a dance teacher.  Or 

21   maybe all.  

22                "I really like to help people and 

23   animals, especially those in need.  I like to 

24   help animals and people in need; helping them is 

25   the right thing to do.  I like helping any animal 


                                                                1170

 1   and all the people around the world that need 

 2   support."  

 3                Mr. President, Olivia's superpower 

 4   is embracing who she is, which is why today I ask 

 5   you to please recognize and acknowledge Olivia 

 6   Ekizian to the chamber.

 7                ACTING PRESIDENT BENJAMIN:   To

 9   the Senate.  We extend to you all of the 

10   privileges and courtesies of this house.  

11                Please rise and be recognized.
